EPC releases two new white papers on GaN power conversion
Monday 14th September 2026
Technical papers examine 800 VDC power delivery for AI infrastructure and integrated 100 V GaN power stages for robotics, drones, and motion control 
Efficient Power Conversion (EPC) has published two new technical white papers addressing critical power-conversion challenges in two rapidly evolving markets: AI data centres and high-performance multi-axis motor drives.
The first white paper, 'GaN-Based Power Delivery in AI data centres: High-Density Power Conversion Architectures from 800 VDC to Point-of-Load' examines the transition toward 800 VDC distribution as AI racks move from tens of kilowatts toward hundreds of kilowatts and megawatt-scale compute clusters. At 800 VDC, a 200 kW rack requires only one-sixteenth of the current of a 48 V distribution bus, reducing conductor size, I²R losses, and cooling requirements. 
The paper explores three architectures for converting 800 VDC to 50 V, 12.5 V, and 6.25 V rails, with particular focus on modular Input-Series, Output-Parallel (ISOP) LLC converters. By dividing the high-voltage input among multiple modules, the architecture enables low-voltage GaN FETs with a better Figure of Merit, when compared to higher-voltage devices, to perform high-ratio conversion at high switching frequencies. 
Practical results demonstrate the performance potential: an 800 V-to-50 V implementation reaches 98.6 percent peak efficiency, while the EPC91123 800 V-to-12.5 V converter achieves 98.2 percent peak efficiency in an 8 mm profile. A 6 kW 800 V-to-6.25 V architecture reaches 98 percent peak and 97 percent full-load efficiency. 
“As GPU power continues to increase, power conversion must move closer to the processor while minimising conversion stages,” said Jason Zhang, Vice President of DC-DC Marketing and System Engineering at EPC. “Gen 7 GaN combined with modular ISOP architectures provides a practical path from an 800 VDC backbone to the very low bus voltages and extremely high currents required by next-generation AI processors.”
The second white paper, 'From Device to Platform: EPC23108/09/10/11 100 V Integrated GaN Power Stages Simplify Multi-Axis Motor Drive Design', addresses the increasing complexity of motor drives used in humanoid robots, drones, surgical robotics, and precision-motion systems. 
EPC’s EPC231xx family integrates high- and low-side eGaN FETs, gate drive, level shifting, control interface, and protection functions into a monolithic GaN 100 V ePower™ Stage IC. The accompanying EPC91128–EPC91131 three-phase BLDC/PMSM inverter platforms give engineers a complete environment to evaluate current capability, sensing, protection, thermal performance, and different PWM interfaces. 
The platforms operate across a recommended 14–80 V range (48 V typical) and support switching frequencies from 20 to 150 kHz. Complementary PWM versions maximise control flexibility, while single-PWM-input-pin versions reduce control-line count and wiring complexity—an increasingly important advantage as robotic systems scale to dozens of motors. 
“In multi-axis robotics, power density is only part of the challenge,” said Marco Palma, VP Motor Drive Marketing and System Engineering at EPC. “Integration must also simplify control, protection, sensing, thermal management, and wiring. The EPC231xx family and its evaluation platforms give engineers a validated starting point that can be replicated efficiently across many motor axes.”

content_text:
HS Hyosung Unit to Invest 1.2 Trillion Won in Ulsan Silicon Anode Plant
Three-Phase Expansion in Ulsan-Mipo Industrial Complex Through 2030 to Reach 20,000 Tons a Year
Joint Venture With Belgium's Umicore Marks Group's First New Business After Spinoff
Society | Published 2026.09.14. 11:29:26 
| By Jang Ji-seung jjs@sedaily.com 
| Summary | Save 
A A A 
Ulsan Mayor Kim Sang-wook and Lee Ki-soo, chief executive of HS Hyosung Energy Solution Korea, sign a memorandum of understanding on investment in a new silicon anode material plant for secondary batteries at Ulsan City Hall on Nov. 14. Photo courtesy of Ulsan City ULSAN — HS Hyosung Energy Solution Korea, a joint venture set up by HS Hyosung Group with Belgium-based Umicore, has chosen Ulsan as its production base for next-generation battery materials. The company will invest a combined 1.2 trillion won ($860 million) through 2030 to build silicon anode production capacity.
The city of Ulsan said on the 14th that it signed a memorandum of understanding on the new silicon anode plant at the mayor's office in city hall, with Ulsan Mayor Kim Sang-wook and HS Hyosung Energy Solution Korea CEO Lee Ki-soo in attendance.
Under the agreement, HS Hyosung Energy Solution Korea will build a large-scale production plant in three phases on a site in the Ulsan-Mipo National Industrial Complex. Silicon anodes offer higher energy density and faster charging than conventional graphite anodes, making them a key material for extending the driving range of electric vehicles and shortening charging times.
The investment will be carried out in stages through 2030. In the first phase, the company will spend 300 billion won to complete its first plant, MPK-1, with annual capacity of 5,000 tons by the first quarter of 2028. In the second phase, it will invest another 300 billion won to add 5,000 tons of annual capacity between the first quarter of 2028 and the third quarter of 2029. In the final phase, it will spend 600 billion won from the first quarter of 2029 to the third quarter of 2030 to add 10,000 tons of annual capacity. Once the third phase is complete, total annual capacity will reach 20,000 tons.
HS Hyosung Energy Solution Korea said it will give priority to hiring Ulsan residents during both construction and operation of the plant to help create local jobs. The city will provide administrative support, including expedited permits and approvals, to keep the project on track.

HS Hyosung Energy Solution Korea said on the 14th it will sign an investment agreement with Ulsan City to build a new plant to produce silicon anode material. Hydro all aboard for railcar recycling effort
The global aluminum producer is working with Siemens Mobility to recycle aluminum from end of life railcars.
Hydro calls the Train2Train project a demonstration of its commitment to low-carbon aluminum and circular economy, showing how collaboration across the value chain can keep valuable materials in circulation.
Photo courtesy of Norsk Hydro ASA 
By
Brian Taylor, Senior Editor 
Published September 11, 2026
Listen to article 
/ 
Recycled-content aluminum producer Norsk Hydro ASA says it is working in collaboration with several other companies in Europe to recycle aluminum recovered from decommissioned trains and then produce new rail industry components.
Hydro, which is based in Norway and has aluminum melt shops in Europe and the United States, says it is working alongside rail industry supplier Siemens Mobility, Germany-based metals recycling firm TSR Group and Austria-based steelmaker Voestalpine on the Train2Train project.
In a pilot study that is part of the project, Hydro will melt recycled aluminum from decommissioned trains at its facility in Ghlin, Belgium. 
The aluminum comes from TSR Group, which has dismantled the rail vehicles and separated aluminum from steel with the aim of recycling the metals into new rail parts. Hydro receives the recyclable aluminum, while Voestalpine receives the ferrous scrap.
After being melted, the aluminum scrap will be processed into extrusion billets, which will be used as input material at a Hydro extrusion facility in Harderwijk, Netherlands. 
Hydro calls the Train2Train project a demonstration of its commitment to low-carbon aluminum and the circular economy, showing how collaboration across the value chain can keep valuable materials in circulation.
“Aluminum can be recycled repeatedly without losing its properties,” says Piotr Chmielewski, a vice president with Hydro Extrusions Europe. “By combining recycling expertise, digital traceability and manufacturing capabilities, we can create new opportunities for circular solutions in the rail industry. This project builds on Hydro’s ambition to accelerate the transition towards a more circular and low-carbon aluminum industry.”
Hydro says it supplies a variety of aluminum products for the rail industry, supporting manufacturers with “lightweight, durable and recyclable materials for applications including train structures, interiors and components.”
The Train2Train project aims to demonstrate that the materials from a decommissioned train can be recovered, recycled and reborn into a new one. 
In the United States, Sweden-based steelmaker SSAB has collaborated with metals recycler Alter Trading, St. Louis, and railcar builder Greenbrier Companies, Lake Oswego, Oregon, in a project that establishes a similar loop .
Hydro  says, “At a time when global supply chains are under increasing pressure, gaining greater control over material flows is becoming increasingly important. The project brings together the full value chain, from dismantling and recycling to material processing and manufacturing, with each partner playing a critical role in creating a transparent and circular material loop.”

title: Chemours, DuPont, Corteva reach $590M settlement with NC over PFAS lawsuits - Raleigh News & Observer
query: ("Chemours" OR "The Chemours Company") ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-09-01 before:2026-10-01
content_text:
Chemours, DuPont, Corteva reach $590M settlement with NC over PFAS lawsuits
By Lily Carey 
Updated September 10, 2026 5:10 PM 
Key Takeaways
AI-generated summary reviewed by our newsroom.
Read our AI Policy. 
Chemours, Corteva, and DuPont reached a $590 million PFAS settlement in NC.
The deal sends $380 million to 11 local authorities hit by PFAS pollution.
DuPont and Corteva will create a $135 million reserve fund for ongoing work.
The three chemical companies that dumped forever chemicals into North Carolina’s rivers for decades have reached a $590 million settlement to resolve several lawsuits in the state.
The settlement, announced Thursday, is the “largest state environmental damages recovery in North Carolina history,” N.C. Attorney General Jeff Jackson said Thursday. It also resolves a state lawsuit against the three companies — Chemours, DuPont and Corteva — that’s dragged on since 2020.
“Roughly 3.5 million North Carolinians currently drink water with PFAS levels above federal health standards in drinking water,” said Reid Wilson, secretary of the N.C. Department of Environmental Quality. “That’s one out of every three people in this state, and this is not just numbers; these are people and families and communities. So this is a really urgent issue because everyone expects and deserves that when they turn on the tap, they’re going to get clean, healthy drinking water.”
North Carolina has been seeking damages from the three companies since 2016, when officials discovered that Chemours had been knowingly discharging forever chemicals, known as PFAS, from its Fayetteville Works industrial plant in Cumberland County and into the Cape Fear River. Drinking water contaminated with PFAS can lead to cancers and developmental issues; the chemicals are extremely difficult to filter from water, and can remain in the human body indefinitely.
The N.C. DEQ had secured a $1.2 billion consent order against Chemours in 2019, and part of Thursday’s settlement will require DuPont, Chemours’ former parent company, to continue funding the cleanup and well testing efforts that started under that consent order if Chemours goes bankrupt.
DuPont had owned the plant since the 1970s before spinning Chemours out into its own company in 2015, but DuPont and Corteva, another one of its offshoots, are still legally liable for pollution at the Fayetteville plant.
Work continues on container tanks at the Chemours plant in a file photo from Nov. 28, 2018. The tanks were installed as measures to reduce PFAS emissions. Melissa Sue Gerrits Carolina Public Press 
What’s in the $590M settlement
Under the settlement, Chemours, DuPont and Corteva will pay a total of $455 million to North Carolina authorities over the next 15 years. $380 million will be paid to 11 local authorities that were impacted by the companies’ PFAS pollution, while another $75 million will be paid to the state. Chemours will pay for half of the $455 million, and DuPont and Corteva will pay the other half.
On top of that, DuPont will also establish a $135 million reserve fund. That’s because Chemours, which was spun out of DuPont in 2015, faces a “real risk of bankruptcy,” Jackson said.
If Chemours does go bankrupt, that reserve fund will act as a “backstop” to make sure that DuPont can cover the full costs of the 2019 consent order, Wilson said.
While it’s not immediately clear what the money will be used for, money from the 2019 consent order has been used to install water treatment systems, sample residential wells, and install pollution control technology and a physical barrier wall at Fayetteville Works.
A spokesperson for Jackson told The N&O that the state will use $55 million of its $75 million from this settlement for the new Emerging Contaminant Mitigation Fund that was created this year by state lawmakers.
The 11 local authorities getting settlement payments are Bladen, Brunswick, Columbus, Cumberland, New Hanover, Robeson and Sampson counties, and the Town of Wrightsville Beach, City of Lumberton, Village of Bald Head Island and Lower Cape Fear Water and Sewer Authority.
After EPA settlement, leaders say NC deal is stronger
Thursday’s announcement comes just over two months after the EPA and the federal Department of Justice reached their own $450 million settlement with Chemours — a deal that North Carolina leaders decried as being too weak.
The EPA settlement, announced in June, resolved lawsuits over Chemours’ PFAS pollution in Fayetteville, as well as at other plants in New Jersey and West Virginia. But while federal officials pegged the settlement at $450 million, North Carolina will only end up receiving an estimated $2 million annually from that deal for the next 15 years, Jackson said Thursday.
“We were hoping that the EPA would take this seriously, but they failed,” Jackson said. “They did a slap on the wrist for... DuPont and Chemours. That was unacceptable. We knew we were going to have to take the lead.”
Chemours told The N&O last month that it was giving less money to North Carolina in the EPA settlement because it already had existing cleanup efforts in the state. Jackson, Gov. Josh Stein and other state leaders pointed to the settlement as a sign that the EPA was less willing to hold polluters like Chemours accountable under the leadership of Trump appointee Lee Zeldin.
Local cleanup, Chemours expansion still lie ahead
While Thursday’s settlement holds Chemours accountable, it’s “not the end of the story,” said Jean Zhuang, an attorney for the Southern Environmental Law Center.
Chemours is still planning an expansion of its Fayetteville Works plant, and while the state has taken steps to curb PFAS pollution at the plant, it hasn’t stopped it entirely.
“While this settlement would help clean up existing pollution, we have to stop the tap ... and part of that means denying the permit for Chemours’ expansion,” said Cori Bell, a senior attorney for the Natural Resources Defense Council.
When asked about the expansion, Wilson told The N&O Thursday that the DEQ “[does] not currently have a pending application from Chemours for... an air quality permit to expand their operations.” According to DEQ’s website, Chemours has submitted an application for a new air quality permit, but DEQ had deemed their application incomplete, and has not received a full application.
DEQ still maintains its full permitting authority under the settlement, Wilson noted — in other words, they can still deny Chemours’ air quality permit expansion if they want to.
Zhuang also said that while this settlement gives “a significant amount of funds for local municipalities who might need it,” the $380 million divided among the 11 local authorities may not be enough to fully clean up PFAS pollution hotspots.
Cleaning up polluted water systems and piping in clean water supply can be an expensive task. Thursday’s news conference took place at the Gray’s Creek Water Project in Cumberland County, which is delivering clean water to two elementary schools and “more than 200 to 300 homes” directly near the Fayetteville Works plant, according to Cumberland County executive Kirk deViere. A sign at the Gray’s Creek site showed that the EPA provided over $9 million for the project.
For local leaders, the next step is taking PFAS control efforts “from the courtroom to the community,” deViere said Thursday.

The N&O maintains full editorial control of the work. If you would like to help support local journalism, please consider a digital subscription, which you can get here .

Boeing to lead eVTOL jamming and spoofing research in Spain
By Web Team 10th September 2026 3 Mins Read 
Share 
LinkedIn 
Twitter 
Facebook 
Email 
Image: AdobeStock 
Boeing Aerospace Spain is to lead a three-year research project aimed at detecting and countering satellite-navigation jamming and spoofing that threatens autonomous air taxis and other advanced air mobility aircraft.
The Validation of Airspace Integration Applications and New Technologies (VARIANT) project brings together Boeing Aerospace Spain (BAS), Boeing’s digital airspace subsidiary SkyGrid and Austrian telecom software firm Dimetor to tackle interference with global navigation satellite systems (GNSS). It will integrate Dimetor’s NAVSentry platform, which uses artificial intelligence to monitor, detect and alert against jamming and spoofing across advanced air mobility (AAM) operations.
The consortium also includes safety consultants ANZEN Engineering, AI Methods and QCentroid Labs, the Carlos III University of Madrid, ANSP ENAIRE, the Polytechnic University of Madrid and Spanish air traffic management (ATM) R&D body CRIDA as subcontractors. It is partly funded by the Community of Madrid’s technological innovation directorate.
eVTOL aircraft and cargo drones could fly low and possibly autonomously in dense urban areas, relying almost entirely on GNSS for navigation in signal-hostile environments. Without a pilot to notice a fault, precise and trustworthy positioning becomes a systemic safety requirement as more aircraft share the same low-altitude airspace.
Jamming floods the signal environment with noise, causing a loss of position that the aircraft can at least detect. Spoofing broadcasts false but plausible signals, so the aircraft keeps reporting a position that is simply wrong, which in an uncrewed eVTOL can propagate undetected through the navigation system.
Rather than deploying dedicated ground receivers, NAVSentry uses existing national telecom networks, as mobile base stations already rely on GNSS for timing and act as passive interference sensors. Aggregating data from tens of thousands of these across a country creates a real-time, wide-area interference-monitoring grid without new hardware.
Dimetor says the approach gives city-scale coverage that fixed receivers cannot, showing where interference is occurring and how it is evolving so operators can reroute traffic before an aircraft enters an affected zone. The platform has already been deployed and tested on military sites.
VARIANT will assess how the detection service applies to AAM operations – including flight planning, contingency management and surveillance – across the different phases of flight, using high-fidelity simulations and real data gathering in Madrid. Alongside interference detection, it will also address ground-based traffic surveillance, local weather monitoring and vertiport resource management.
The work supports SkyGrid’s aim of building ground-based digital ATM for autonomous operations in complex urban airspace. Boeing Aerospace Spain and SkyGrid bring aerospace integration and certification expertise, while Dimetor contributes the NAVSentry platform and its telecom-data partnerships.

content_text:
Amkor Technology increases Arizona semiconductor campus investment to $12bn
By
Alexa Hornbeck 
| Published: 10-Sep-2026 
Design & Build 
Containment 
The semiconductor packaging and test services provider will add 60,000 sqm of cleanroom space to its Arizona campus, taking the site’s total cleanroom footprint to approximately 93,000 sqm
Amkor Technology is expanding its planned investment in a new advanced semiconductor packaging and test campus in Arizona to approximately $12bn, as customer commitments drive the addition of a second phase.
The company said demand has surpassed the 33,000 sqm of cleanroom capacity planned for Phase 1 of the campus.
Phase 2 will add a further 60,000 sqm, bringing the total cleanroom area across the site to around 93,000 sqm. 
The project is being developed as a multi-phase semiconductor manufacturing campus in Peoria, Arizona, with capabilities spanning wafer bump, probe, assembly and test.
Amkor said the expansion will increase the scale of advanced packaging manufacturing in the US, with the combined phases expected to support a workforce of more than 3,500 Arizona-based employees. 
The campus is intended to become the first US outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) production site providing advanced packaging at high volume, offering customers a domestic turnkey manufacturing platform.
Construction of Phase 2 is expected to begin in late 2027, with completion targeted for the end of 2029. The wider campus covers approximately 170 acres, allowing for further expansion in response to customer demand. 
Amkor originally broke ground on the Arizona campus in October 2025, when the planned investment stood at $7bn across two phases. The project was initially planned to provide more than 750,000 sq ft of cleanroom space. 
The latest expansion follows a series of developments around Amkor’s US advanced packaging strategy.
In June, the company announced a 10-year agreement with TSMC covering advanced packaging and testing services in Arizona, while in July it announced a multi-year partnership with NVIDIA supported by a $1.5bn advanced packaging and development agreement.
“This next phase reflects the confidence our customers have placed in Amkor, the critical role advanced packaging plays in enabling the future of semiconductor innovation, and the strategic importance of our Arizona campus," said Kevin Engel, President and CEO of Amkor Technology.
The Arizona campus will support semiconductor applications including artificial intelligence, data centres, smartphones, automotive and wearable devices.

content_text:
Nexeon raises £100 million to expand its UK silicon anode operations
Posted September 9, 2026 by Chris Ruoff & filed under Newswire , The Tech . 
Oxfordshire-based silicon anode developer Nexeon has closed a £100-million ($133-million) investment round, completed by a £52.6-million ($70-million) commitment from the UK’s National Wealth Fund . The Korea Development Bank and Honda Xcelerator Ventures, Honda’s open innovation investment program, also came in as new investors. The round follows the $170 million Nexeon raised in 2022 in a round that included Ingevity.
The National Wealth Fund’s financing will go toward a UK-based pilot manufacturing facility, R&D work and an expansion of Nexeon’s advanced manufacturing technology unit. A pilot line is where a materials supplier proves out a process at intermediate scale and makes the qualification samples cell manufacturers test before anyone commits to full production volumes.
Silicon holds far more lithium per gram than the graphite it replaces in a conventional lithium-ion anode, but it expands as it takes up that lithium, and containing the expansion over hundreds of cycles is the central engineering problem for silicon anode materials . Nexeon says its materials raise cell energy density, cut charging times and extend EV driving range.
Nexeon already makes silicon-carbon materials at a volume production plant in Gunsan, South Korea. The company has said it picked the site for pipeline supply of monosilane gas, a key precursor for the material, and for its proximity to Asian cell producers. The plant is designed so that additional reactors can be installed to scale output, according to the company.
“This investment is a strong endorsement of Nexeon’s technology and our role in enabling the next generation of lithium-ion batteries. The National Wealth Fund’s support reflects the strategic importance of our work, not only in advancing battery performance but also in strengthening the UK’s position in the global battery supply chain,” said Scott Brown, CEO of Nexeon.

title: Solvay confirms OneIM talks over strategic European rare-earths business - EU Today
query: ("Solvay" OR "Solvay SA") ("press release" OR "investor relations" OR earnings OR announcement OR investment OR expansion OR acquisition OR partnership OR Korea) after:2026-09-01 before:2026-10-01
content_text:
Solvay confirms OneIM talks over strategic European rare-earths business
by EUToday Correspondents 
September 9, 2026 
written by EUToday Correspondents 
September 9, 2026 
Solvay confirms OneIM talks over strategic European rare-earths business
2K The Belgian chemicals group said in regulated information on 8 September that talks were continuing and that it would provide further information when appropriate. The announcement followed a Reuters report that discussions had been under way since March. OneIM did not immediately comment.
The asset at the centre of the talks is Solvay’s separation operation at La Rochelle in France. The site processes rare-earth materials used in magnets and other advanced manufacturing. Solvay describes the business as part of its broader Special Chem portfolio, which also includes fluorine products; figures for the combined portfolio should not be treated as rare-earth revenue alone.
The potential partnership comes as European governments seek alternatives to Chinese processing. Separation capacity is more difficult to build than a mine because it requires specialised chemistry, waste controls, qualified staff and long-term feedstock contracts. A change in ownership or financing could therefore affect Europe’s industrial plans even if Solvay continues to operate the plant.
Financing a supply chain
Solvay has signed a letter of intent with Brazil’s Viridis Mining and Minerals to source rare-earth feedstock for La Rochelle from the Colossus project. The arrangement is targeted for 2028 and remains subject to a definitive agreement and project development. It covers neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium, terbium and other materials that can feed magnet production.
Viridis said OneIM would invest up to $75 million and become a cornerstone investor in its Brazilian project. That is financing for the upstream development, not proof that European separation capacity has already expanded. Solvay has also discussed a €15–20 million La Rochelle expansion, with heavy rare-earth separation targeted for autumn 2026.
The possible OneIM partnership could provide capital or a different ownership structure for those plans. Solvay has not disclosed a valuation, timetable or the form of any investment. Its statement makes clear that talks may end without an agreement.
EU Today has previously covered Brussels’ plans to build a critical-minerals stockpile. The Solvay discussions show the industrial side of that policy: stockpiles can provide insurance, but processing plants require steady feedstock, financing and customers over many years.
The next formal development will be a company announcement if the parties reach binding terms. Until then, La Rochelle’s capacity, the Viridis timetable and the 2028 supply target remain separate pieces of a proposed chain. Solvay’s notice gives no valuation or closing date, so the talks cannot be treated as a completed sale.

The Arizona campus will include wafer bumping, probing, assembly and testing capabilities, creating a domestic manufacturing platform for advanced semiconductor devices.
Phase 2 construction planned for 2027
Construction of Phase 2 of the campus is expected to start late in 2027, with completion scheduled for the end of 2029.
The expansion will boost manufacturing capability of the campus and provide employment opportunities for over 3,500 Arizona-based employees for Phase 1 and Phase 2. The company noted that the 170 acre campus has been built to enable additional expansion of capacity based on customer requirements.
Amkor president and CEO Kevin Engel said that the next phase shows customer confidence in Amkor and increasing significance of advanced packaging for semiconductor manufacturing.
The campus will create a turnkey domestic manufacturing platform for customers with a combination of several stages of advanced packaging and testing services in the U.S.
Arizona campus strengthens U.S. domestic semiconductor manufacturing
Amkor’s Arizona campus project is part of its plan for building the first advanced semiconductor outsourced assembly and test production facility in the U.S.
Development of the campus is also a step towards building more domestic manufacturing facilities for semiconductors. The company has stated that its Arizona campus is complementary to front-end wafer fabrication in the state, which creates an opportunity to link wafer fabrication with advanced packaging and testing within the U.S. semiconductor manufacturing value chain.
In June 2026, Amkor and TSMC entered into a 10-year deal to enhance advanced semiconductor packaging capabilities in Arizona. As per the agreement, TSMC will be purchasing advanced packaging and testing services from Amkor for addressing increasing demands for advanced semiconductor devices used in high-performance computing, artificial intelligence, and advanced electronics.
In May 2026, Amkor expanded the physical area of its campus development project with an acquisition of 67 additional acres of land adjoining its existing 104-acre campus, resulting in a total of about 171 acres of land. Additional land has been acquired for future expansions.
Construction of the first manufacturing facility is underway
Construction of the first manufacturing facility is underway. Amkor has stated that construction of foundation is advancing towards steel construction and Phase 1 is still on target for completion in 2027.
The enlarged campus will be able to provide advanced packaging and testing services for artificial intelligence, high-performance computing, automotive and communications applications. Amkor’s investment program in 2026 also includes substantial spending on capital expenditures for its Arizona campus with the company estimating about $2.5 billion to $3 billion for 2026.
With Phase 2 added in Arizona, Amkor will build a much larger U.S. advanced semiconductor manufacturing campus, expanding domestic cleanroom capacity to meet growing demand for chip packaging.
Additionally, the semiconductor manufacturing buildout is also gaining momentum beyond the United States. In the Netherlands, ASML has broken ground on its new BIC North industrial campus in Eindhoven , launching a multi-phase development that could eventually span approximately 350,000 square meters and accommodate up to 20,000 workplaces.

Infineon and SolarEdge extend collaboration
Wednesday 9th September 2026
Companies extend collaboration into solid-state circuit breaker (SSCB) technology 
Infineon and SolarEdge Technologies have extended of their collaboration to advance solid-state circuit breaker (SSCB) technology for high-voltage DC distribution in AI and hyperscale data centres. 
The collaboration addresses a key challenge in the adoption of 800 VDC architecture: Safe operation of increasingly power-dense infrastructure requires a very fast fault-isolation to achieve selectivity while maintaining high efficiency.
The compannies says that the aims is to address a critical gap in the distribution layer between the solid-state transformer (SST) and the compute rack, in order to develop a grid-to-rack solution. SolarEdge is leading the design of the SSCB solution, with Infineon providing its SiC JFET technology at the core of the protection devices.
DC protection presents different engineering challenges to AC designs. Without a natural current zero, mechanical interruption faces challenges with arcing. It is comparatively slow, and as such requires a different approach to circuit protection than conventional AC systems. 
Solid-state circuit breakers are designed to interrupt faults within a few microseconds, with no mechanical contacts to separate, while Infineon's CoolSiC JFET devices are claimed to deliver efficient operation and superior robustness. Together, these capabilities help protect high-value compute equipment and enable more compact, higher-density DC distribution designs.
The collaboration builds on SolarEdge's SST platform ( pictured above ) with Infineon SiC components, first announced in November 2025. The SST is designed to enable direct medium-voltage (13.8-34.5 kV) to 800-1500 VDC conversion at over 99 percent efficiency, collapsing multiple conversion stages into a single solution while reducing physical footprint.

Total investment exceeds 20 billion yuan! New和成 and Susco, two leading enterprises, are stepping up their investment in special engineering plastics.
2026-09-09 08:57:34 
Source:ChemNet 
中文 
Leading chemical giants at home and abroad are simultaneously stepping up their layout in the high-end materials track recently, and the special engineering plastics sector has ushered in a boom in major capacity expansion. Overseas giant Syensqo is deeply cultivating the Asia-Pacific market, while domestic leader NHU has launched a 10-billion-yuan project, with both sides making layouts to seize the incremental demand of high-end materials, accelerating domestic substitution in the industry and reshaping the global competition pattern.
Syensqo expands its presence in the Indian market, doubling high-end composite production capacity by 2028 
On September 3, international materials giant Syensqo announced its Indian capacity expansion plan, it will build a new high-performance aromatic polymer composite production line at its Panoli site, which is scheduled to officially go into production in the first quarter of 2028 . This production line is the first project of its modular composite center to be implemented. Upon completion, it will directly double the existing composite production capacity of the site.
The new production line supports the composite production of multiple high-end special materials such as PPS, PEEK, PPA and PARA , and can flexibly adjust the production structure according to market demand, adapting flexibly to high-end manufacturing orders. Relying on the core advantages of high temperature resistance, corrosion resistance, high strength and light weight, Syensqo's materials are widely used in the high-end automobile manufacturing field.
With the comprehensive localization and upgrading of India's automobile industry, the demand for high-performance engineering plastics continues to rise. This investment not only strengthens Syensqo's local supply and R&D capabilities in India, consolidates its supporting advantages in the global automobile manufacturer supply chain, but also further improves its regional business layout in the Asia-Pacific region and taps into the incremental market of high-end materials in multiple industries.
NHU launches a 10-billion-yuan project, comprehensively expanding special engineering plastics production capacity 
While foreign capital is laying out the Asia-Pacific region, NHU, the domestic leading fine chemical enterprise, is making heavy efforts. On August 29, NHU's 10.5-billion-yuan special new materials project was officially signed and landed in Shangyu, Zhejiang . After completion, the project will greatly increase the domestic special engineering plastics production capacity, drive the upgrading of the regional new materials industry cluster, and empower the development of emerging industries such as low-altitude economy and embodied intelligence.
New materials business has become the core growth segment of NHU. Its products cover high-end categories such as PPS, PPA, IPDA and HDI, which are widely used in automobile, electronic and electrical appliances, industrial environmental protection and other fields. In the first half of 2026, the company's revenue was 13.129 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 18.28%; among them, the revenue of new materials business was 1.166 billion yuan, a year-on-year increase of 12.31%, with steady growth momentum.
In terms of capacity layout, NHU has built a complete special materials industry chain system.
PPS sector , the company currently has a production capacity of 22,000 tons, with a total approved production capacity of 30,000 tons, and the remaining 8,000 tons/year capacity project is advancing steadily. It is the only domestic enterprise that can stably produce multi-grade PPS and achieve mass production of bio-based PPS.
Nylon materials sector , the 10-billion-yuan nylon integration project in Tianjin has basically completed the civil construction, and equipment is being installed one after another. The first phase will be put into production in 2027, with a planned annual output of 100,000 tons of adiponitrile, 100,000 tons of hexamethylenediamine and 140,000 tons of nylon 66. The second phase plans to have a nylon 66 production capacity of 400,000 tons; the long-chain special nylon project in Shandong base has completed the environmental impact assessment publicity, and has broken through the core technology of nylon 12.
Special isocyanate sector , the 20,000-ton IPDI project of HA Phase II has started smoothly. The existing products such as HDI, IPDA and ADI have achieved mass production and entered the high-end market. Coupled with the 110,000-ton aliphatic isocyanate project approved this year, the production capacity of high-end fine materials continues to be released.
Emerging industries drive demand explosion, accelerating domestic substitution process 
As a core high-end chemical material, special engineering plastics include more than ten high-end categories such as PPS, PPA, PEEK and PI, and are key basic materials for electronic communication, new energy vehicles and precision manufacturing. Although the unit price is relatively high and the overall consumption value accounts for only 1.8%, driven by tracks such as the AI industry, low-altitude economy, new energy vehicles and high-speed communication, the demand for high-end special materials continues to be booming.
According to institutional data, the annual composite growth rate of China's special engineering plastics market will reach 7.2% from 2023 to 2028, it is estimated that the consumption volume will exceed 246,000 tons in 2028 . At present, domestic leading enterprises continue to break the overseas technical monopoly by virtue of technological breakthroughs and large-scale capacity expansion, and the import substitution in the medium and high-end fields of special engineering plastics is accelerating in an all-round way, and the industry is ushering in long-term growth dividends.

Amkor Technology Announces Phase 2 of Arizona Advanced Packaging and Test Campus; Expands Investment to $12 Billion
Business Wire 
September 8, 2026 3 min read 
AMKR 
-10.70% 
Strong customer commitments support 60,000 square meter expansion of U.S. advanced packaging capacity 
TEMPE, Ariz., September 08, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )--Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR), a leading provider of outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services, today announced phase 2 of its Arizona Advanced packaging and test campus. Driven by strong customer commitments that have surpassed the 33,000 square meters of cleanroom capacity planned for phase 1, the phase 2 expansion is expected to add 60,000 square meters and bring the campus to approximately 93,000 square meters of cleanroom space. The expansion increases the project's planned investment to approximately $12 billion. 
Designed from the outset as a multi-phase project, Amkor's Arizona campus, which includes wafer bump, probe, assembly and test capabilities, is being developed to support long-term demand for advanced semiconductor packaging and test services in the U.S. Phase 2 expands manufacturing scale, and together with phase 1 is expected to support a workforce of more than 3,500 Arizona-based employees. 
"This next phase reflects the confidence our customers have placed in Amkor, the critical role advanced packaging plays in enabling the future of semiconductor innovation, and the strategic importance of our Arizona campus," said Kevin Engel, president and chief executive officer of Amkor Technology. "As chip architectures become more complex, customers need a trusted partner that can deliver at scale with the quality, technology leadership and operational discipline required for their most advanced products, and it is critical to have that capacity in the U.S." 
Amkor's Arizona campus is the first OSAT production site in the U.S. for advanced packaging in high volume, giving customers access to a full domestic turnkey manufacturing platform. Construction of phase 2 is anticipated to begin late 2027, with completion expected by the end of 2029. Amkor's Arizona 170-acre campus allows for further expansion as needed to support customer demand. 
About Amkor Technology, Inc. 
Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR) is the world's largest U.S. headquartered OSAT and is a global leader in outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services. With a strong track record of innovation, a broad and diverse geographic footprint and solid partnerships with lead customers, Amkor delivers high-quality solutions that enable the world's leading semiconductor and electronics companies to bring advanced technologies to market. The company's comprehensive portfolio includes advanced packaging, wafer-level processing, and system-in-package solutions targeting applications for smartphones, data centers, artificial intelligence, automobiles and wearables. For more information visit amkor.com .

Two companies' longstanding collaboration expands into High-NA EUV and next-generation semiconductor manufacturing
Engineers at ASML inspect a High-NA EUV lithography system. (ASML) 
Samsung Electronics and Dutch manufacturer of chip equipment ASML said Tuesday they would expand their long-standing partnership on next-generation lithography technologies critical to producing advanced AI chips.
The expanded partnership between South Korea’s largest chipmaker and ASML focuses on high numerical aperture extreme ultraviolet lithography and advanced photomask solutions, areas expected to become increasingly important as chipmakers push the limits of semiconductor scaling.
As part of the expanded partnership, Samsung will help develop a next-generation 12-inch photomask platform for High-NA EUV manufacturing.
Photomasks act as templates that transfer circuit patterns onto semiconductor wafers during the chipmaking process. While the industry has traditionally relied on 6-inch photomasks, larger 12-inch formats are expected to improve manufacturing efficiency by supporting more advanced patterning processes and reducing complexity in future semiconductor production.
The move comes as global chipmakers face mounting challenges in developing smaller and more powerful semiconductors. As artificial intelligence applications drive demand for high-performance computing, companies are racing to secure technologies that can deliver greater processing capability while improving production efficiency.
High-NA EUV is widely viewed as the next major step in semiconductor lithography. The technology builds on existing EUV systems by improving resolution capabilities, allowing manufacturers to create more precise circuit patterns for future generations of logic and memory chips.
For Samsung, adopting High-NA EUV is closely tied to its competitive strategy in the memory semiconductor market. The company plans to apply the technology to future DRAM production as it seeks to strengthen its position in areas such as high-bandwidth memory, which has become a key component in AI infrastructure.
The latest cooperation also reflects a relationship between Samsung and ASML that has developed over more than a decade.
The two companies have worked closely since EUV lithography was still considered a major technological challenge for the semiconductor industry. As traditional methods approached physical limits, EUV emerged as a breakthrough technology capable of enabling more advanced semiconductor manufacturing.
ASML, the world’s leading supplier of semiconductor lithography equipment, has become a critical player in the global chip supply chain through its EUV systems. The company remains the only manufacturer capable of supplying commercial EUV lithography machines used by leading semiconductor producers worldwide.
Samsung was among the early semiconductor companies to adopt EUV technology and has continued expanding its use across both memory and foundry operations. The company’s experience with EUV manufacturing has positioned it as one of the key players in the transition toward next-generation semiconductor processes.
"The AI era is transforming the semiconductor industry and increasing the importance of technological innovation across the entire value chain," Samsung Electronics Vice Chairman and CEO Jun Young-hyun said. "By further strengthening our collaboration with ASML, we are helping lay the foundation for the next generation of AI and semiconductor innovation."
ASML President and CEO Christophe Fouquet also emphasized the importance of cooperation between equipment suppliers and chip manufacturers as the semiconductor industry enters a new phase of technological competition.
"As the industry enters a new era driven by artificial intelligence, close collaboration with our customers becomes even more important," Fouquet said.
The partnership highlights a broader shift in the semiconductor industry, where access to advanced manufacturing technologies has become a strategic advantage. As demand for AI-related chips continues to reshape the market, Samsung and ASML are seeking to strengthen their positions by advancing the technologies that will define the next generation of semiconductor production.

Regional Capabilities 
 
September 7, 2026
London —Dentons has advised the National Wealth Fund on its investment of up to US$70 million (£52.6 million) in Nexeon Ltd, a leading developer of advanced silicon-based battery materials. The investment will support the expansion of the company's domestic operations, strengthening the UK's battery supply chain, creating jobs and boosting growth.
The National Wealth Fund's investment forms part of Nexeon's latest funding round, which is expected to raise a total of US$133 million (£100 million). It will support the development of Nexeon's UK-based pilot manufacturing facility, enabling the company to scale its advanced manufacturing technology unit and research and development capabilities. 
The transaction was led by Projects Partner Torquil Law and Corporate Partner Adam Knowles , with assistance from Corporate and Projects associates Murray Newell , Mel Mahon  and Karina Chopra  and other Dentons UK colleagues from its Projects, Corporate, Environment, Competition, Employment and Pensions, and Technology, Media and Telecoms teams.
Torquil Law commented: "We are delighted to have advised the National Wealth Fund on this investment, which will help decarbonise supply chains, boost place-based investment, and strengthen sovereign capabilities - supporting all three of the National Wealth Fund’s strategic ambitions."

GeoCue Elevates Survey-Grade Drone Mapping with Ouster's BABA-Compliant Native Color Rev8 Digital Lidar
Provided by Business Wire Sep 2, 2026, 4:00:00 PM 
GeoCue Elevates Survey-Grade Drone Mapping with Ouster's BABA-Compliant Native Color Rev8 Digital Lidar 
Pairing survey-grade precision with Ouster’s 256-channel Rev8 OS1 Max lidar, GeoCue’s latest TrueView lineup sets a new benchmark for U.S. drone surveying 
Ouster, Inc. (Nasdaq: OUST) (“Ouster” or the “Company”), a leader in sensing and perception for Physical AI, announced a strategic partnership with GeoCue, a premier provider of drone mapping payloads and software, to integrate Ouster’s native color Rev8 OS1 Max digital lidar into GeoCue’s TrueView product line. The collaboration pairs GeoCue's TrueView 1 payloads and LP360 software with Ouster's digital lidar to deliver survey-grade data to the utility and infrastructure industries.
This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260902576177/en/ 
Ouster Rev8 OS1 Max on GeoCue's TrueView drone payload, mapping a construction site (product rendering).
GeoCue is expanding its TrueView lineup to include options featuring the Ouster Rev8 OS1 Max, which is Build America, Buy America Act (BABA)-compliant. These new options give customers who have domestic production requirements a high-performance solution without technical compromises.
Ouster and GeoCue selected the Rev8 OS1 Max after joint flight testing and firmware tuning in Huntsville, Alabama. "We are moving America's drone surveying onto American sensing by pairing our TrueView payloads with Ouster's Rev8 OS1 Max," said Frank Darmayan, CEO of GeoCue. "This transition allows us to offer our customers a compliant, high-performance solution that delivers the survey-grade data they depend on for critical infrastructure monitoring and large-scale mapping projects."
The Rev8 OS1 Max brings four key advantages to GeoCue's utility and infrastructure customers:
Superior Precision: A smaller spot size and tighter beam allow TrueView payloads to resolve thin objects such as power lines and structural edges.
Expanded Operational Range: Longer range (200m at 10% reflectivity) clears altitude restrictions around utility corridors, letting operators fly higher while maintaining data quality.
Native Color Integration: The Rev8 OS1 Max captures native color in addition to 3D lidar data, so every point arrives inherently aligned to its color. Alongside the dual cameras in every TrueView payload, that gives LP360 an additional RGB reference for registering camera imagery to the point cloud, enabling tighter sensor fusion.
Density at Speed: 256 channels in 2K and 4K modes keep point density high even at fast flight speeds, supporting long-corridor surveys by propeller and fixed-wing aircraft.
"Our partnership with GeoCue is a testament to how native color digital lidar can serve as the bedrock for physical AI applications that have a profound impact on infrastructure and public safety," said Ouster CEO Angus Pacala. "By integrating our Rev8 OS1 Max sensor, we are providing the survey-grade precision and reliability required to empower the next generation of drone mapping professionals."
Experience the Rev8 OS1 Max for Drone Surveying at Commercial UAV Expo 
Ouster will be showcasing its Rev8 OS1 Max native color digital lidar at Booth #1653 during the Commercial UAV Expo in Las Vegas (September 1-3, 2026). Attendees can stop by the booth for live hardware demonstrations or schedule a meeting with our technical team.
About Ouster 
Ouster (Nasdaq: OUST) is a leader in sensing and perception for Physical AI across industrial, robotics, automotive, and smart infrastructure. With a unified platform of high-performance digital lidar, cameras, AI compute, sensor fusion and perception software, and AI models, Ouster delivers solutions that improve quality of life in the physical world. Headquartered in San Francisco, CA, Ouster has a global presence serving thousands of customers with offices in the Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. For more information about our products, visit www.ouster.com , contact our sales team , or connect with us on X or LinkedIn .
About GeoCue 
GeoCue brings geospatial professionals advanced drone, mobile and terrestrial surveying equipment, point-cloud processing software, workflows, training and support for high-accuracy LiDAR and imagery mapping. With TrueView LiDAR and imaging sensors and LP360 point-cloud processing software, GeoCue provides complete solutions for successful data collection, processing, quality control and deliverable creation. GeoCue meets customers where they are in terms of technology, adoption, budget and resources while supporting their continued growth. To learn more about GeoCue, visit www.geocue.com .

National Wealth Fund backs Nexeon’s sodium battery tech with £53 million 
The money brings the Oxfordshire-based company’s latest investment round to £100 million (US$133 million), with additional investments from the Korea Development Bank and Honda Xcelerator Ventures.
Will Norman , Senior Reporter , Informa September 2, 2026
schedule 2 Min Read 
Nexeon claims that its technology enables faster charging and higher energy density in battery systems, with a variety of applications including electric vehicles. Image: Nexeon 
The UK National Wealth Fund has invested £52.6 million (US$70 million) into silicon anode battery technology startup Nexeon. 
The money brings the Oxfordshire-based company’s latest investment round to £100 million (US$133 million), with additional investments from the Korea Development Bank and Honda Xcelerator Ventures. 
The National Wealth Fund said the investment supports Nexeon’s “continued scale-up and commercialisation activities”. The funds will go towards Nexeon’s plans for a pilot UK manufacturing facility and its ongoing research and development (R&D) efforts. 
Nexeon is developing silicon anode technology for energy storage systems, which it said can enable the production of higher energy density lithium-ion batteries. The company operates a mass production facility in South Korea and has a research base in Japan, as well as its Oxfordshire headquarters. 
Nexeon claims that its technology enables faster charging and higher energy density in battery systems, with a variety of applications including electric vehicles (EVs). 
Related: Foresight invests in 40GWh LDES cap-and-floor winning pumped hydro project in Scotland 
"Companies like Nexeon show the strength of British innovation,” said chancellor of the exchequer John Healey. “And if we are serious about growth, we must be serious about backing British businesses like this with conditions for them to start, scale and succeed here in the UK, as the National Wealth Fund are doing here.” 
Oliver Holbourn, chief executive officer of the National Wealth Fund, added: “Our investment in Nexeon is fully aligned with our mission to support clean energy innovation and economic growth. Backing advanced battery technology is key to building a globally competitive EV supply chain in the UK”. 
Scott Brown, chief executive of Nexeon, said the investment was a “strong endorsement of Nexeon’s technology and our role in enabling the next generation of lithium-ion batteries”. 
Back in January, the National Wealth Fund revealed plans to facilitate £100 million of investment into UK clean energy , prioritising battery manufacturing and energy storage alongside grid upgrades and carbon capture projects. 
Industries minister Blair McDougall said: "Hot on the heels of a £130 million investment into net zero vehicle technologies, our Modern Industrial Strategy is doubling down on frontier industries like batteries to help businesses like Nexeon grow their business, create skilled jobs and drive good growth right across the UK.” 
There have also been some efforts to onshore solar supply and manufacturing in the UK. Great British Energy invested in Naked Energy , a solar thermal company, last month. 
Related: Ofgem: Locking assets out of LDES cap-and-floor support would have ‘perverse outcome’

content_text:
Nexeon raises £100m as National Wealth Fund invests
Abingdon firm is developing silicon anode materials which will help to reduce charging times and extend range of electric vehicles
Share: 
Listen to article 
EnviroTech Investment Manufacturing Battery startup Nexeon has secured backing from the National Wealth Fund as part of a £100 million funding round. 
The National Wealth Fund has committed £52.6m, with other new investors in the round including the Korea Development Bank and Honda Xcelerator Ventures. 
Nexeon, headquartered in Abingdon near Oxford, is developing silicon anode materials which enable production of higher energy density lithium-ion batteries, helping to reduce charging times and extend the range of electric vehicles. 
The investment round supports the company’s continued scale-up and commercialisation activities and marks another key milestone in the pathway to high-volume manufacturing and global customer adoption. 
The National Wealth Fund’s financing will support Nexeon’s development of a UK-based pilot manufacturing facility, directly supporting their research and development activities and allowing the expansion of its advanced manufacturing technology unit, creating a number of new highly skilled jobs. 
By investing in innovative battery technologies and expanding local manufacturing capacity, the Fund says its investment will help to decarbonise supply chains, boost place-based investment and strengthen sovereign capabilities — supporting all three of the National Wealth Fund’s strategic ambitions. 
Honda Xcelerator Ventures is the global open innovation program of the Honda Motor Co. Ltd., and invests in technologies shaping the future of mobility and electrification. The Korea Development Bank is a leading policy bank in South Korea, focused on supporting industrial innovation and global expansion of Korean-linked manufacturing ecosystems. 
£100m competition backs British AI firms to fix public services 
Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey MP said: “Companies like Nexeon show the strength of British innovation. And if we are serious about growth, we must be serious about backing British businesses like this with conditions for them to start, scale and succeed here in the UK, as the National Wealth Fund are doing here. That’s how we’ll get good growth and jobs in every postcode.” 
Oliver Holbourn, CEO of the National Wealth Fund, said: “Our investment in Nexeon is fully aligned with our mission to support clean energy innovation and economic growth. Backing advanced battery technology is key to building a globally competitive EV supply chain in the UK, as the thought-leadership paper we recently published identifies. 
“This investment will help unlock private capital, support high-value jobs and drive regional growth, while helping to position the UK at the forefront of innovation in the battery sector.” 
Dr Scott Brown (pictured), CEO of Nexeon, said: “This investment is a strong endorsement of Nexeon’s technology and our role in enabling the next generation of lithium-ion batteries. The National Wealth Fund’s support reflects the strategic importance of our work, not only in advancing battery performance but also in strengthening the UK’s position in the global battery supply chain.” 
David Lamb, CFO at Nexeon, added: “We continue to strengthen our shareholder register with the addition of the Korea Development Bank, Honda and the National Wealth Fund. The quality of the Nexeon commercial proposition is reflected in the quality of investors we continue to attract.”

Sumitomo Chemical and Gutenberg Co., Ltd. (“Gutenberg”), which is leading the development of high-speed 3D printers produced in Japan, have jointly developed a liquid crystal polymer (LCP) filament and molding technology for 3D printers that use the FFF method (*1) . The Company will accelerate the development of applications in next-generation fields, including functional components that contribute to advances in semiconductors and physical AI.
3D-printed parts 
Robot hand housing 
In recent years, materials capable of handling complex geometries, achieving weight reductions, and integrating parts have been receiving increased interest across advanced industrial fields. For this reason, design and manufacturing using 3D printers have attracted increasing attention. Amid this trend, there is a demand for not only freedom of design, but also for high functionality in resin materials themselves. LCP is a super engineering plastic that combines heat resistance, high strength, low dielectric constant and low dissipation factor, and excellent dimensional stability. As a material for 3D printers, however, its use has been limited due to difficulties in filament formation and molding.
To address these challenges, Sumitomo Chemical has developed a material design and filament formation technology for LCP suited to additive manufacturing. The Company also collaborated with Gutenberg, which develops, manufactures, and sells industrial 3D printers, to examine the molding process and establish a technology that enables stable molding while controlling the unique molecular orientation of LCP. This technology achieves high thermal conductivity and strength comparable to that of aluminum alloys (*2) , while also maintaining lightweight properties. This makes it possible to create complex shapes that are difficult to achieve with injection molding, while also meeting the needs of low-volume, high-mix production.
Going forward, Sumitomo Chemical will expand its efforts into a wide range of fields, including peripheral components for semiconductor manufacturing, humanoid robot-related components that are expected to be put into practical use as physical AI advances, the communications field, and next-generation mobility fields such as eVTOL (*3) . In addition, the Company will accelerate the development of new applications by advancing evaluations of its filament and molded products in collaboration with customers. The Company plans to begin providing samples of this filament in 2026, and it is also looking ahead to future expansion into the space and defense fields.
Sumitomo Chemical will continue to promote the provision of innovative materials and solutions that support next-generation manufacturing. In doing so, the Company will contribute to the creation of new value and the development of society and industry.
(*1) A 3D printing method in which thermoplastic resin is melted, extruded from a nozzle, and stacked layer by layer. 
(*2) The Company evaluated the fracture strength of LCP and aluminum alloy under certain conditions using a test method compliant with standards set by the International Organization for Standardization. 
(*3) Electric Vertical Take-Off and Landing aircraft, commonly referred to as flying cars.
